newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Dairibord Zimbabwe issue 10 times oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Dairibord Zimbabwe issue 10 times oversubscribed.

text.p: Zimbabwe's first public offer of a state-owned firm, Dairibord Zimbabwe Limited (DZL), was 10 times oversubscribed, the company said in a statement.

It said more than 26,000 new and traditional investors had applied for a stake in the national dairy which was offering 168.3 million shares at a price of Z$1.20 each under a government plan to privatise the company.
"The public has shown great confidence in our company which mirrors the confidence with which Dairibord faces the future," DZL chairman Paddy Millar said in the statement.

A consortium of banks advising DZL on its privatisation said financial arrangements had been put in place for the preferential allocation of shares for large and small-scale milk producers, DZL employees, the National Investment Trust and a technical partner yet to be named.

Under the proposed new share structure, the public would hold 15 percent of the shares while the technical partner would have 10 percent with an option to buy a further 15 percent of the company's equity from a remaining 40 percent stake held by the government.

The state National Investment Trust, formed to promote the government's programme to economically empower the southern African country's majority blacks, large-scale milk producers and DZL employees, would hold 10 percent each while small-scale producers would have five percent.
